Endocrine Control of Energy Metabolism
Energy use in the body is constant, but ingestion of energy-
yielding nutrients is sporadic. Th is means that excess energy 
taken in meals must be stored for later use between meals.
About 1500 kcalories (less than a day’s worth of energy) are 
stored as carbohydrate in the form of glucose (circulating in
blood) and as glycogen (liver and muscle cells). Carbohydrate 
is the body’s primary energy source and the preferred source
of energy for brain cells. Excess carbohydrate (beyond what 
is used for glucose and glycogen) is converted to and stored 
as fat (triglycerides). Fat, the body’s primary energy reser-
voir, can provide about two months’ worth of energy during 
a prolonged fasting period. Fat is stored in adipose tissue in
the form of triglycerides, and also circulates in the blood as
